summary.text:
A posted custom notification. It wraps a native object that knows the notification key, so an
instance recovered with
`CustomNotificationFactory.get()`
or
`getActive()`

after a process restart
behaves like the one returned by
`post()`
The key of the notification, as passed to or generated by
`post()`

Removes the notification from the shade immediately.
Cancels any pending post or update for this notification.

Reads the props currently shown by the notification from the active notification, so they
include changes made by button presses inside the notification.

Rejects when the notification is no longer active, for example after dismissal or cancellation.

summary.text:
Renders the layout with new props and replaces the notification in place. The notification
does not alert again when
`alertOnlyOnce`
is
`true`

.

Rejects when the notification is no longer active, for example after the user dismissed it or
after
`cancel()`

. Post it again in that case. Also rejects when the notification is canceled
while the update renders, or for the same reasons as
`post()`
, such as an invalid
`color`
The new props for the layout function.

Posts and manages custom notifications that share one layout.

summary.text: The key passed to or generated by
`post()`

Returns every active notification posted with this layout, including notifications posted
before a process restart.
Renders the layout and posts the notification. Posting with the
`id`

of an active notification
replaces that notification in place.

Rejects in these cases:
- Notifications are disabled for the app.
-
`channelId`

names a channel that does not exist.
-
`smallIcon`

names a drawable that does not exist.
-
`color`
is not in
`#RRGGBB`
or
`#AARRGGBB`

format.
- The layout returns no
`collapsed`

section.
- The post is canceled before rendering finishes.

at a

The collapsed row shown in the notification shade. The system gives it about 64
density-independent pixels (dp) of height.

The expanded view shown when the user expands the notification. The system gives it up to
256 dp of height. When omitted, the system derives the expanded view from
`collapsed`

The heads-up view shown when the notification peeks over the current screen. The system gives
it about 88 dp of height. When omitted, the system reuses
`collapsed`

. The channel importance
decides whether a heads-up view is shown at all.
